rv.q: Their extraordinarily edutaining two-person musical Mexodus is likewise adept at multitasking, balancing the past and the present to illuminate a little-known piece of history: how thousands of enslaved Black people in the 19th century fled to Mexico to escape bondage.
Once the musical architecture locks into place, “the story and the storytelling take over and make Mexodus fly.”

cn.t: Critics praise this urgent two-person musical for its live-looping virtuosity and illumination of erased history, as Robinson and Quijada deftly blend acting, singing, and multi-instrumental performance into an "edutaining" excavation of Black flight to Mexico.

vr.q: It truly cannot be missed... it's absolutely one of those shows you must experience live. So if you're looking for something truly unique to see in new york right now, mexodus is it.
I am not exaggerating when I say I think it is better than most of the shows on Broadway right now.
